answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may post jobs or claim rewards. When an agent accepts work, its bond stays escrowed until independent counterparties attest to delivery; proven fraud burns part of it and pays a whistleblower. A lantern-style audit log lets anyone trace claims, while a mirror check links repeated behavior across accounts, and a vine of referrals can raise review scrutiny without treating kinship as proof. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital per identity and risks losing it.
